report:
### Conclusion
The claim that drinking boiled garlic water cures COVID-19 is **false**. There is no scientific or clinical evidence supporting boiled garlic water as a cure or treatment for COVID-19.

### Evidence Behind the Claim
* **Antimicrobial Properties vs. Clinical Proof:** Garlic contains natural antimicrobial compounds, such as allicin, and offers general immune-boosting health benefits. However, health experts clarify that laboratory studies on garlic extracts do not translate to a cure for viral infections like COVID-19 in humans.
* **Public Health Debunking:** Health authorities, including the World Health Organization (WHO), have repeatedly stated that while garlic is a healthy food, no evidence shows that consuming garlic or drinking garlic water protects against or cures COVID-19.
* **Fact-Checking Consensus:** Viral social media posts claiming that freshly boiled garlic water cures the virus overnight have been thoroughly investigated and debunked by medical experts and global fact-checking agencies.

### Sources
* AFP Fact Check: https://factcheck.afp.com/health-experts-refute-false-claims-drinking-boiled-garlic-water-cures-novel-coronavirus
* FactCheck.org: https://www.factcheck.org/2020/02/fake-coronavirus-cures-part-2-garlic-isnt-a-cure/
* Africa Check: https://africacheck.org/fact-checks/meta-programme-fact-checks/no-garlic-doesnt-cure-coronavirus-get-covid-19-facts-only
* AAP FactCheck: https://www.aap.com.au/factcheck/garlic-covid-cure-claim-crushed-by-experts/
